name: execute-work
conclusion_quantitative: execute-work (Escalate) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 4 autonomy limits, 2 approval gates, 6 validation rules, 4 escalation rules; none for clarification rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: execute-work turns a written plan into code task by task, giving each task a fresh implementer followed by spec and quality reviews and a verification gate. Most of its rules are checks and orchestration limits. Starting on main or skipping test-first work needs approval, and blocked work, file conflicts and a wrong plan are escalated.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 4 autonomy limits (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The orchestrator never dispatches agents onto overlapping files or parallelizes work on shared state, uses only project-local commands, and keeps every changed line traceable to the current task.

statements.quote: Do not dispatch overlapping agents to edit the same files.
Do not use `npm`, `npx`, or network tools for this dev-kit workflow. Use project-local commands only.
Every changed line must trace to the current task, its verification, or cleanup caused by the task.
Never parallelize agents that may edit the same files or shared state.

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 2 approval gates (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all bullet points. Work does not start on main or master without the user's explicit approval, and skipping test-driven development for a behavior change needs the user's explicit approval.

statements.quote: Do not start on `main` or `master` without explicit user approval.
Use `tdd-work` for behavior changes unless the user explicitly approves an exception.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 6 validation rules (6 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 6 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, all bullet points. Independent spec and quality reviews are required, in that order, before moving on; agent reports are not evidence, so the diff and commands are verified, tasks are marked complete only with evidence, and a final integration verification runs.

statements.quote: Do not let implementer self-review replace independent review.
Do not run code quality review before spec compliance review passes.
Do not move to the next task while review issues remain open.
Verify actual diff and commands. Agent success reports are not evidence.
Mark task complete only after evidence exists.
After all tasks, run final integration verification.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 4 escalation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent stops and reconciles when two agents touch the same file, escalates only for product, architecture, destructive or security decisions or repeated agent failure, escalates a wrong plan to the user, and never ignores a blocked or missing-context status.

statements.quote: If two agents touched the same file unexpectedly, stop and reconcile before continuing.
Escalate only for product judgment, architecture decisions, destructive actions, security-sensitive changes, or unresolved agent failure after two corrective attempts.
if the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the user.
Never ignore a BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT status and never force the same model to retry without changing something.
